Mira Chen: FYI handing over an ongoing alert that started ~2h ago. emb-queue p99/99.9 in eu-west-1 still elevated after the initial scale. Primary for the last 2h has been Alex R., Jon P. has been secondary for mitigation testing. I'm the last on-call before you - leaving at 07:30 UTC. TL;DR: customer impact limited but persistent error spikes for small subset of customers (~0.3% requests fail with 502/timeout).

Oncall Bot: INCIDENT: emb-queue-p99-eu-west1 | Pager triggered 3320000100 | Severity: P2 (customer-facing intermittent errors)

Alex R.: current state — we've autoscaled the dedicated pool (x2 nodes) and flipped routing to fallback-model-v2 for low-latency traffic. That cut average latency but p99 is still spiking due to backend queue head-of-line on a small shard. We suspect a KV cache thrash and one worker node hitting GPU memory pressure.

Jon P.: log snippets showing repeated OOM-ish GC messages + eviction churn. pasted logs: ```[2026-03-15T05:22:31Z] worker-12 GPU mem spike 98% -> process restart; [2026-03-15T05:22:32Z] kvcache: eviction count +480/s; [2026-03-15T05:24:00Z] request backlog 320 -> 1200```

Sasha K.: quick checks done: replacing worker-12 returns it to pool but spike recurs after ~10m. We enabled routing by shard to move traffic away from shard-7 which is suspected. No errors in upstream model load.

Mira Chen: Mitigations in progress (what to continue):
- Keep fallback-model-v2 routing for new heavy requests (already active)
- Disable prefetch on shard-7 nodes to reduce KV churn: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/internal/nodes/shard-7/prefetch -d '{"enabled":false}'`
- If p99 stays > 1.5s after 10m, run temporary soft-eviction: `opsctl kv evict --shard shard-7 --ratio 0.25` (see runbook link below)
- If GPU mem pressure continues, scale +1 node and set `node-termination-probation=5m` so we don't immediately reassign heavy load back.

Jon P.: Customer impact assessment — active errors mainly for small enterprise customers using long-context embeddings. Not a global outage. Support notified with incident summary. We should keep communications low-noise for now and escalate only if error rate >0.5% sustained 10m.

Oncall Bot: RUNBOOK: emb-queue-throttle-runbook v3.2 — https://go.redwood/ops/runbooks/emb-queue-throttle

Mira Chen: Who's next primary? I assign @Alex R. to finish mitigations for the next hour (primary), @Jon P. stays secondary for infra actions, @Sasha K. on rotation for customer comms if needed. If anything blocks escalation (cannot isolate shard or persistent OOM), page SRE lead.

Alex R.: Acked. Will monitor for 40m from now and iterate. My watchlist: 1) KV eviction rate, 2) GPU mem % on shard nodes, 3) request backlog per router.
Quick checks to run on handoff:```bash
# backlog per router
curl -s https://ops-api/internal/routers/eu-west-1/backlog | jq .
# kv eviction metrics
promql 'sum(rate(kv_evictions_total{region="eu-west-1"}[1m])) by (shard)'
# GPU mem per node
opsctl node metrics --region eu-west-1 --metric gpu_memory_used_percent
```

Sasha K.: I'll keep a short support note ready with status + approximate ETA. If we need to escalate, message on #incidents and ping @oncall-lead.

Mira Chen: Known gaps to call out for next shift:
- We don't have an automated prefetched disable rollback — it's manual and needs a ticket afterwards for post-mortem cleanup.
- Runbook step for soft-eviction is slightly brittle for multi-tenant shards; only apply if eviction reduces backlog in 5m.
- No confirmed root cause yet; deferring to infra team for deeper mem profiling.

Jon P.: If you inherit this, first action after ack: check for repeated node restarts in the last 30m. If >2 restarts on the same node, isolate it and reroute.

Mira Chen: Handoff summary (copy into your notes): primary=Alex R., secondary=Jon P., support=Sasha K., severity=P2, impacted ~0.3% requests (enterprise long-context), mitigations active=fallback routing, prefetch disabled on shard-7, auto-scale +1 if mem pressure persists. Runbook link above. My contact for quick follow-up: @Mira Chen. Leaving now — good luck, and ping me if escalation needed :thumbsup:
